sections.brief: Coricancha gold taken for Atahualpa's ransom 1533, Santo Domingo built on its walls (post-1650 building); Inti Raymi: last royal festival 1535 (popular date), Toledo's 1572 ban on Inca-cult ceremonies (press account), 1944 revival; Corpus Christi on the solstice (Dean); Punchao seized 1572, Túpac Amaru executed 24 Sept 1572 despite clergy's pleas, Julien's trail to Philip II's inventory; Taki Onqoy (Olvera 1564, Albornoz, scale disputed: Varón/Guibovich); Qoyllurit'i (UNESCO 2011). Figures: time

Tonatiuh and the Fifth Sun, Huitzilopochtli; sacrifice and the huei tzompantli (600+ skulls, 20,000 figure disputed); Templo Mayor razed 1521, church built from its stones, cathedral 1573-1813, rediscovered 1978; Sun Stone buried on Montúfar's order (Durán), found 17 Dec 1790, displayed on the cathedral 1791-1885; Maya codices (four survive; Dresden astronomy; Landa July 1562, link vt34); Codex Borgia in the Vatican Library since 1902; survivals: voladores (UNESCO 2009), Chamula Our Father Sun/Christ (Gossen), Lacandon; church-orientation claim graded. Figures: compare (destroyed vs survived)

Sol Invictus and CTh 16.10.10-12 (link vt21, vt33); Philae (394/452 inscriptions, closure c.535-537 by Narses, Dijkstra); Goa temple orders 1541/1546/1567 (link vt34_goa); Sun Dance banned by the US Interior Department 1883 (Teller, Price; no congressional act) until AIRFA 1978, Canada 1895-1951; Japan: Amaterasu, Christianity banned 27 Jan 1614, Shimabara, Kakure Kirishitan, 1873; Zeitgeist 'all saviours are sun gods' graded (Forbes, Goldberg); labelled interpretation (sun as inner light) with counter-readings. Figures: compare (suns of the world: people, deity, who suppressed, when, document, what survived)
